Hi Kyle,

Thanks again for the great discussion this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call:

Goals:
- Surface real-time account balances and transaction intel inside FinApps' admin UI.
- Allow agents to invoke sanctioned backend actions (refund, flag-account) via an LLM-driven UI.

Integration touchpoints we flagged:
- SDK setup & auth (server-to-server vs user-level)
- Routing: latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive paths, fallback models
- Structured output / tool-calling: tool definitions and schemas
- Embeddings & reranker for semantic search and result scoring

Open items / asks from your side:
1) Can your security team share preferred auth pattern (API key, OAuth2 with JWT, or mTLS)?
2) Expected QPS and typical request size (tokens) so we can size batching and rate limits.
3) Procurement timeline & PO contact (if moving forward).

Attachments I'm sharing: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (integration patterns) and proposed-map.png (high-level routing + tools). I've also pasted a short tool-calling pattern summary below for quick reference.

Tool calling (short):
- Define each tool with a strict JSON schema (inputs + output types).
- Prefer orchestrator to call multiple scoring/ranking tools in parallel, then aggregate-safe outputs.
- Retries: idempotent tools get 2 retries with exponential backoff; non-idempotent actions require explicit user confirmation.

Next steps I propose:
- Share SDK quickstart + sample tool schema (by EOD) — Marcus will draft the sample.
- Security questionnaire follow-up (Anita?) — please loop in procurement/security.
- Schedule architecture call (30-45m) with engineering (Ben + Marcus) — proposed times below.

Thanks —
Marissa

Kyle / Anita,

Thanks — answers inline below and links to docs:

Auth:
- Recommendation: OAuth2 with short-lived JWTs for user-scoped tool invocations (refunds, sensitive reads). Use mTLS for the highest-sensitivity server-to-server paths if your infra supports it. API keys are OK for internal backend-to-backend flows but we don’t recommend them for user-scoped actions.
- Doc: https://drive.google.com/redwood/auth-patterns (SDK supports both flows).

Tool schemas & hosting:
- Yes — host canonical JSON Schemas in your repo or a shared drive. We recommend a small tools manifest: name, id, input_schema, output_schema, idempotent (bool), timeout_ms.
- We’ll attach a sample SDK manifest (sdk-quickstart.md) and a sample tool schema in the repo we share.

Parallel tools & orchestration:
- Pattern we use: fan-out enrichment in parallel (embeddings lookup, fraud score, enrichment API), then a deterministic aggregator step that applies safety filters and rankers.
- If any enrichment is non-blocking, return partial responses with explicit status and a follow-up job.

Retries & error handling:
- Idempotent tools: retry 2x with exponential backoff, then fallback to cached result (if available).
- Non-idempotent tools (charges, refunds): surface to user for confirmation and log a tentative-dry-run before live call.
- For transient failures: return structured error {code, message, recoverable: bool, suggested_action}. Our SDK maps these into typed exceptions.

Embeddings + reranker:
- Use a lightweight semantic reranker for top-N results (embedding similarity) and then run a small cross-encoder reranker if you need higher precision for top-3.
- Cache embeddings for entities and use a TTL based on update frequency (e.g., 24-72 hours).

Rate limits & batching:
- Default hosted rate limits are 120 reqs/minute per API key; we provide burst windows and configurable rate policies for Dedicated. Batching is supported in SDK to reduce per-token cost. Marcus will provide more precise numbers based on your expected qps.

I’ve attached the SDK quickstart and a short sample manifest inline. If that looks good, let’s lock a 45m architecture call — I’m available Wed 4/21 10:00-12:00 or Thu 4/22 14:00-16:00 PT.

Sample tool manifest (example):
{
  "tools": [
    {"id": "fraud_score", "name": "FraudScore", "input_schema": {"account_id": "string", "tx_id": "string"}, "output_schema": {"score": "number", "reason": "string"}, "idempotent": true},
    {"id": "refund", "name": "IssueRefund", "input_schema": {"account_id": "string", "amount": "number"}, "output_schema": {"status": "string"}, "idempotent": false}
  ]
}

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Marcus’ samples and a proposed MAP.
